qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Rural store density and farm-savvy customer service create local convenience switching barriers in secondary/tertiary markets, but TSCO lacks structural pricing power above inflation. Passing on price increases leads directly to unit volume contractions, traffic declines, and customer cross-shopping at Walmart, dollar stores, local farm co-ops, and e-commerce (Chewy/Amazon).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (REJECT – G3 Moat & Pricing). Specialty rural lifestyle retailer with strong brand recognition and high ROIC (~14-18%), but lacks genuine pricing power above inflation. Unit volumes and transaction counts stall when prices rise, as seen in flat comparable store sales (+0.1% FY24, +1.2% FY25, -1.0% to 0% FY26 guidance) and stagnant net income plateaued at ~$1.10B across 2022-2025. Operating margins compressed to 8.0-8.3% due to rural wage inflation and SG&A pressures.
qualitative.evidence: FY2024 revenue of $14.88B and net income of $1.10B; FY2025 revenue of $15.52B and net income of $1.10B (zero net income growth across 4 consecutive years). Comp store sales moderated from pandemic highs to +0.1% in FY24, +1.2% in FY25, and guided -1.0% to flat in FY26 (Q3 2026 at +0.4%). Free cash flow conversion remains weak at ~58% in FY24 ($637M FCF / $1,101M NI) and ~68% in FY25 ($741M FCF / $1,096M NI), well below the 80% threshold due to $675M-$700M annual capex. Balance sheet carries $1.83B in long-term debt plus >$3.5B in operating lease liabilities across 2,390+ stores.
